title: Technical Specifications of 160mm Ridged Pipe: Selection Guide
html:
Introduction to the importance of the mainline in irrigation systems

In every drip or micro-sprinkler irrigation system, the selection of the mainline plays a decisive role in overall performance, system durability, and pump energy management. One of the most commonly used sizes in medium to large-scale systems is the 160 mm threaded pipe which has gained attention among farmers and irrigation engineers due to the appropriate balance between pressure, cost, and flow velocity.

Applications of 160 mm threaded pipe in farms

This pipe size is typically used to convey water from a reservoir or main channel to lateral lines in medium to large farms. Due to the presence of flanges or threaded connections at both ends, installation and connection to other irrigation equipment such as solenoids, diaphragm filters, or globe valves is much easier. This feature increases operational efficiency in locations where quick access is required for filter or valve repair and replacement.

Technical specifications of 160 mm threaded pipe

Familiarity with precise technical specifications is the first step in correct selection. 160 mm polyethylene (PE) pipes are available with different wall thicknesses, each designed for a specific pressure range.

Wall thickness and pressure rating

The most critical technical parameter is the pipe wall thickness (SD - Standard Dimension Ratio). For common pressure levels in drip irrigation systems (typically 1 to 6 bar), pipes with SD 11 or 12 are suitable choices. As the working pressure increases, pipes with a thicker wall should be used to prevent sudden bursts.

Material composition and UV resistance

Quality PE pipes are manufactured from linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE), which offers high resistance to cracking and abrasion. Another important factor is the inclusion of anti-UV additives in the polymer blend. Since these pipes are typically installed outdoors under direct sunlight, resistance to ultraviolet radiation protects the pipe's useful life. Low-quality pipes may become hard and brittle after one or two summer seasons.

Flange connection and thread type

Threaded or flanged fittings at both ends of the pipe must be manufactured from brass or high-quality ABS. Whether these connections are disposable or reusable depends on the thread type (Right-hand or Left-hand). Standardizing the threads ensures that the pipe is fully compatible with standard industrial irrigation fittings to prevent leaks.

Selection guide based on application

In order to use the guide for calculating quantities and planting doses for various crops, you should know that the designed flow rate for different farms impacts the selection of pipe size. For example, if you are looking to optimize water consumption for crops with deep roots , maintaining pressure in the main pipe becomes twice as important.

Determining the required flow rate

To prevent pressure drop, the flow rate from the 160 millimeter pipe must not exceed the allowable velocity. Ideally, the water velocity inside the main pipe should not exceed 2.5 meters per second. If your system flow rate is very high (for example, for high-water-requirement crops such as tomatoes), you may need to use two 160-meter pipes in parallel or select a larger size.

Auxiliary equipment and filtration

The main pipe serves as the connection point for filters, solenoids, and pressure manifolds. Using threaded pipe allows filtration equipment to be connected to the main line without the need for additional intermediate parts. For Understanding benefits and calculating fertilizer dose in irrigation, fertilizer injection systems should also be placed at appropriate points on the main pipe to ensure uniform mixing.

Practical tips for installing and maintaining threaded pipe

Correct installation determines half the useful life of the pipe. Below are the key points to consider when purchasing and implementing a drip irrigation system.

  1. Deep burial or surface installation?: If the 160-meter pipe is placed on the surface as the main line, it must always be covered with UV-protective material or buried in the soil (15-20 cm). Uncovered laser pipes degrade quickly.
  2. Installation angle of fittings: When connecting to a flange, the pipe must not be stretched or twisted. Using an appropriate junction box or tee fitting for branch connections prevents breakage at the connection point.
  3. Line flushing: At the beginning of each growing season, open one end of the pipe to allow accumulated sediment to be flushed out with a strong flow. This prevents clogging of downstream emitters.

Also, when planning irrigation for moisture-sensitive crops such as onions, uniform pressure distribution along the entire main line is essential. If the line is very long, significant pressure drop may occur at the end, in which case using Hagen-Poiseuille calculations or standard HFR tables to determine flow rate and pressure is necessary.

Comparison of threaded pipe and welded pipe

Feature160 threaded pipe160 welded pipe
Connection typeFlange/boltThermoplastic welding
Implementation costLower (in small/medium-sized farms)Higher (Welding machine required)
Installation SpeedFastAverage (Installation and cooling)
Leakage Resistance DurabilityDependent on O-Ring QualityExcellent (Permeable connection)
Most Suitable ApplicationMobile systems, greenhouse farms, lateral linesPermanent mainlines, high pressures

In most cases, 160 mm threaded pipe Due to the low cost of tools and simple connections, it is a popular choice, unless your system operates at very high pressures above 10 bar, in which case welded pipes and more robust industrial fittings are recommended.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Why is a 160 mm pipe not recommended for small farms?

In farms smaller than 1 hectare, the total flow rate of the system is usually lower, and the use of a 105 or 125 mm pipe is sufficient. A 160 mm pipe under these conditions causes a reduction in water velocity and increases the likelihood of sedimentation inside the pipe.

What is the length of each pipe segment?

Polyethylene pipes are usually supplied in 20 or 50-meter segments. Spliced 160-mm pipes from longer segments are more common due to the higher cost of transporting long lengths.

Can a 160 mm pipe be connected directly to a drip line?

It is recommended to treat the 160 mm pipe as the main lateral. Drip lines should be connected to the main pipe via T-connectors or nipples, not directly without a tee.

Summary

Selection 160 mm threaded pipe For drip and tape irrigation systems, this is a smart choice for medium-to-large farms. By adhering to technical specifications such as appropriate wall thickness, UV resistance, and correct installation, these pipes deliver efficient performance for years without the need for replacement. For comprehensive crop and water planning, it is better to use the guide for calculating seed rates and planting spacing for various crops to ensure that all aspects of your irrigation system are optimized.
